author: Briana Byus
title: Porterville teen tied to online extremist group, tech expert warns of online dangers - NewsBreak
text:
By Briana Byus ,
2 hours ago PORTERVILLE, Calif. ( KSEE/KGPE ) – A Porterville teenager is facing up to 69 years in prison for felonies related to an online extremist group.
“A parent shouldn’t be surprised by anything that can happen online,” CEO of Helpdesk Tech in Fresno, J. Colin Petersen, said.
The DOJ says 19-year-old Tony Long is federally indicted on six charges , including two counts of animal crushing and sexual exploitation of a minor.
Prosecutors say Long did all of this while working with what they call a “Nihilistic Violent Extremist” criminal organization.
“These dirtbags don’t start with technology. They certainly don’t start with another person’s well-being. They start by tapping into loneliness and a search for answers,” Petersen said.
Petersen says all teenagers search for a place to belong, and the internet creates the path of least resistance to that community.
He says online predators capitalize on that.
“They’ll tap into a teenager’s sense of wanting to be on the inside, or some sort of secret group or understanding,” Petersen said.
However, he says those secrets come with a price. Criminals will manipulate teenagers into committing crimes or sharing explicit photos, which sends the victim into a spiral of shame and isolation.
His advice to parents is to “Have an open relationship with your children about what they are doing online. Be curious about the information that they’ve found online, if they’ve found some ‘secret path’ to something.”
He adds that it is not overbearing to restrict phone use in your child’s bedroom; it’s wise.
His message to any teenager who feels trapped because of their online choices is to “Take those things out of dark spaces and shed light on them. Light is the most powerful sanitizer we have.”
He says, no matter how much shame you feel, it’s never as bad as it seems, and hiding your online activity will only make it worse.
